name: Mortar Vector Siege
description: A player-held VR MORTAR vs a drone swarm. Grab the tube, TILT your hand to set the launch angle, HOLD the trigger to charge force, then RELEASE to lob a RigidBody shell on a ballistic arc. A live parabola, a green velocity arrow, a red gravity arrow, and a ground AoE ring preview where the shell will fall — computed analytically, so the preview never waits on physics. The shell detonates on the earlier of floor-contact or analytic impact, area-bombing every flying drone inside the splash radius. Indirect-fire sibling of the direct-fire `hl_turret_vectors`: there you point AT the target, here you aim a parabola so its FOOT lands on it. Desktop/headless: auto-aims at a roaming drone and auto-fires so a capture shows the arc + a shell + the swarm.
theoreticalGrounding: v0 = aim_dir * force; p(t) = p0 + v0*t + 0.5*g*t^2. Hand tilt sets direction, charge time sets magnitude — together they fix where the parabola crosses the floor. Gravity is not the obstacle to the shot, it IS the shot. Indirect fire makes the velocity vector and the constant gravity vector legible as the curve they sum to.

mortar_vector_siege.name: Mortar Vector Siege
mortar_vector_siege.description: Grabbable mortar tube (XRToolsPickable) on a base, over a ground disc, facing a wandering swarm of flying drones. Aim = -tube.basis.z; muzzle Marker3D = p0. Hold trigger to charge _force (min->max over ~1.2s), release to fire a RigidBody shell (gravity_scale=g/9.8, contact_monitor, continuous arc). Live velocity/gravity arrows + dotted parabola + analytic floor AoE ring. Shell detonates on floor contact OR y<=floor_y, popping drones within aoe_radius. Grip or cooldown reloads the cosmetic shell. Scoring on drone_destroyed. DNA: min_force, max_force, gravity_magnitude, aoe_radius, drone_count.
mortar_vector_siege.qfep_connection: F_force: launch velocity + constant gravity = a parabola whose foot is the strike. Indirect fire teaches the vector sum as a felt aim, not a watched arc.

dna.default: foresight=parabola, vectors=sum - byte-for-byte the 3 shipped placements. parabola emits the same dotted arc from the same 96-step walk AND leaves the AoE ring and its impact dot lit, which is what the mortar has always drawn; sum is the green velocity arrow beside the red gravity arrow, both already built in _build_vector_indicators. The two component arrows are never instantiated at the default, so the scene tree and the capture AABB are the pre-promotion ones, and the floor-crossing solve runs unconditionally at every value so _predicted_impact_world, the drone target-lock and every fired shell are unchanged.
dna.was: the prediction was always the WHOLE solution at once - the dotted parabola and the 2.2 m splash ring and the impact dot, all three hard-coded in _update_trajectory_and_aoe with no way to hand the player less; and the launch was always one arrow beside one gravity arrow, hard-coded in _update_vector_arrows.
dna.family: the catapult's two words, character for character, shared with catapult / human_catapult / force_pad. This machine is the indirect-fire member: the others throw at something you can see, a mortar aims a parabola so its FOOT lands on a drone the tube is not pointed at, which makes it the purest case the word foresight has. One rung is its own - on a catapult `landing` had to invent a 0.35 m marker because a stone lands on a point, while a mortar lands on an AREA, so the ring already on this floor IS the landing at its true splash radius.
dna.fixture_why: rng_seed pins the swarm: _spawn_one_drone picks every anchor with randf() and the headless auto-aim then aims at the first drone in the list, so an unseeded sweep photographs five different arenas and reads the difference as an axis. sky_dome drops the 60 m backdrop sphere, whose 120 m mesh in the union AABB would frame the 0.55 m tube at about one pixel - the six-ways-null table's 'AABB inflated by one far-flung mesh' row. Both default to the shipped behaviour and neither is an axis.
dna.not_an_axis: min_force / max_force / charge_time / aoe_radius / reload_cooldown / drone_count are all MAGNITUDES - turning them makes the same mortar lob further or splash wider, and the charge and the flight are events a still cannot hold at all.
